speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient has a 3-week history of fatigue, difficulty to concentrate, and dyspnea on exertion. He also experiences dizziness and digital pain that improves with cold. He has a long history of smoking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That digital pain relieved by cold is a classic sign of Raynaud's phenomenon, which often accompanies autoimmune conditions. Given your smoking history and these symptoms, have you noticed any skin changes on your fingers or toes, such as swelling, discoloration, or thickening of the skin? Also, have you experienced any joint pain or stiffness?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential, Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).
REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of hands showing Raynaud's phenomenon or sclerodactyly.
